market_context: United States and general English-speaking market
title: Plant-based burger vs. beef burger: nutrition compared

seo.title: Plant burger vs. beef burger: protein, fat and sodium
seo.meta_description: Compare a current Beyond Burger with 90/10 ground beef on the same 100 g basis.
seo.search_intent: Compare plant-based and beef burger nutrition

excerpt: A formulated plant burger can come fairly close to beef in protein but differ sharply in saturated fat and sodium. Normalizing both to 100 g makes the trade-offs clearer.
content_html:
A modern plant burger can come quite close to beef in texture and protein, but that does not make its Nutrition Facts panel “the same, only plant-based.” When a current Beyond Burger and raw 90/10 ground beef are normalized to 100 g, the plant patty has slightly less protein and saturated fat, but more sodium and slightly more calories.

Nutrition per 100 g

Beyond BurgerRaw 90/10 ground beef
Calories~204~176
Protein~17.7 g~20 g
Total fat~12.4 g~10 g
Saturated fat~1.8 g~3.9 g
Sodium~310 mg~66 mg before seasoning

Protein is close: beef provides only about 2.3 g more per 100 g. Saturated fat in the plant patty is less than half—about 1.8 versus 3.9 g—while sodium is almost five times higher before any salt is added to the beef.

Plant-based does not automatically mean lower-calorie

The plant burger is about 204 calories per 100 g versus 176 for the beef reference, a difference of roughly 28 calories. That is not enormous in a full meal, but it shows why “plant-based” is not a synonym for “light.”

These patties are formulated to reproduce the juiciness and texture of beef, and added fats are part of how they do it.

The saturated-fat advantage is specific, not universal

In this comparison the plant patty provides about 2.1 g less saturated fat per 100 g. Other meatless burgers use different fat systems, so the result should not be applied automatically to every brand.

Sodium tells a different story

The Beyond patty arrives pre-seasoned at roughly 310 mg sodium per 100 g. Fresh beef starts around 66 mg. Salting the beef narrows that gap, but the practical point remains: much of the plant burger's sodium is already built into the product before cooking.

Micronutrients depend on the food and fortification

Beef naturally supplies vitamin B12, zinc, and heme iron. Plant burgers may contribute iron and other minerals and can be fortified, but formulas differ substantially between brands. They may also provide some fiber, which beef does not.

Which is better?

There is no category-wide answer. In this specific comparison, the plant burger is clearly lower in saturated fat but higher in sodium and slightly higher in calories; beef is slightly higher in protein and has a different micronutrient profile. The bun, sauces, portion size, and rest of the meal can matter just as much as the patty label.

faq.question: Is a plant burger lower in calories?
faq.answer: Not necessarily; this one normalizes to ~204 kcal/100 g versus 176 in raw 90/10 beef.

faq.question: Which has more protein?
faq.answer: The beef reference: 20 versus about 17.7 g/100 g.

faq.question: Which has more sodium?
faq.answer: The plant burger in this example.
